pages.title: Computer science, explained until it actually makes sense
pages.lede: A full written course for IB Computer Science HL, with a logic simulator you can slow down, Python you can run in the page, and diagrams for everything.

pages.title: Boolean algebra
pages.lede: Ordinary algebra with only two numbers in it. Learn a dozen rules and you can shrink a circuit on paper before it is ever built.

pages.title: Circuit builder
pages.lede: A blank canvas and the seven gates. Build anything, toggle the switches, and get the truth table back automatically.
sections: If a wire refuses to connect

pages.title: Real circuits
pages.lede: What gates are actually assembled into: addition, selection, addressing, and memory.
sections: The SR latch: a circuit that remembers extension

pages.code: A1.2.1–A1.2.2 · Representing data · How binary stores data
pages.title: Data representation
pages.lede: Everything in the machine is a number, and every number is a pattern of switches. This is how text, pictures and sound get in and out of that.

pages.title: Data transmission
pages.lede: What the data physically travels along, how it is cut up for the journey, and how the far end knows it arrived intact.

pages.title: Databases
pages.lede: Storing data so that it stays true. Almost every rule in this topic exists to stop the same fact being recorded twice and then disagreeing with itself.

pages.title: Expression lab
pages.lede: Type a Boolean expression. Get it typeset properly, its full truth table, its minterms, its simplest form and its logic diagram.

pages.code: A1.2.3 · Describe the purpose and use of logic gates
pages.title: The seven gates
pages.lede: Each gate is one rule about switches. Learn the seven rules and their symbols and the rest of the topic is bookkeeping.
sections: NAND and NOR can build anything

pages.title: Hardware and operation
pages.lede: What the parts are, what each one does, and the cycle that repeats billions of times a second underneath everything else.
sections: A1.1.2–A1.1.3 The GPU, and why it is different

pages.title: Karnaugh maps
pages.lede: The same simplification as Boolean algebra, except you can see it. Rearrange the truth table so that neighbours differ by one bit, and the answer becomes a shape.
sections: Gray code, and why the order looks wrong
When not to use a map

pages.title: Labs
pages.lede: The parts of the course that are far quicker to understand by fiddling with them than by reading about them.

pages.title: CPU lab
pages.lede: A processor small enough to follow by eye. Step it through the cycle and watch every register.

pages.title: Number lab
pages.lede: Denary, binary, hexadecimal and two's complement, all showing the same value at once.

pages.title: Sampling lab
pages.lede: How a continuous sound becomes a list of numbers, and what each extra bit costs you.

pages.title: Scheduling lab
pages.lede: Give the scheduler some processes and see which algorithm treats them best — and which one starves them.

pages.title: SQL lab
pages.lede: A working relational database in the page. Write queries against it and see the rows come back.

pages.code: A1.2.5 · Construct logic diagrams (up to three inputs)
pages.title: Logic diagrams
pages.lede: Turning an expression, or a sentence, into a drawing an examiner will accept.
sections: Conventions that get you the marks

pages.title: Machine learning
pages.lede: Programs that are not told the rule, but work it out from examples — and the ways that goes wrong.
sections: Overfitting, and why you hold data back

pages.title: Network architecture
pages.lede: How the machines are arranged, who holds the resources, and why big networks are deliberately cut into smaller ones.

pages.title: Network fundamentals
pages.lede: What a network is made of, the layered model that keeps it comprehensible, and the protocols that let machines from different manufacturers agree.

pages.code: A1.3 · Operating systems and control systems
pages.title: Operating systems
pages.lede: The program whose job is to manage all the other programs — and the smaller cousins of it that run lifts, greenhouses and traffic lights.
sections: A1.3.1 What an operating system is for
A1.3.2 The functions of an operating system

pages.title: Reference sheet
pages.lede: Symbols, truth tables and laws, with nothing in between. Built for the night before.

pages.code: EXT · Why speed has a limit
pages.title: Timing and hazards
pages.lede: Gates are not instant. Everything difficult about building fast computers follows from that one fact.
sections: Glitches, and how a correct circuit lies

pages.title: Translators
pages.lede: A processor only understands binary machine code. Everything else has to be translated, and there are two ways to do it.

pages.code: A1.2.4 · Construct and analyse truth tables
pages.title: Truth tables
pages.lede: A truth table is a circuit with nothing left to the imagination: every possible input, and what comes out.
sections: Going the other way: table to expression
Circuits with more than one output

    Sections: Denary, binary and hexadecimal; Negative numbers: two's complement; Representing text; Representing images; Representing sound; Units
/data-transmission/ — Data transmission [A2.3 · Data transmission]
    What the data physically travels along, how it is cut up for the journey, and how the far end knows it arrived intact.
    Sections: Choosing a medium; Wired media; Wireless; Packet switching; Detecting errors; Keeping transmission private
